properties.name: A rule the project follows is recorded with its consequence stated, and a violation is computed rather than remembered
properties.statement:
A project's own conventions — how it merges, who may sign off, what the build refuses — are part of its design and must be recordable as design, with the CONSEQUENCE of breaking each one stated by the person whose project it is. A rule whose power over the build was never chosen by anybody is not a rule the design can act on.

⚠️ STATUS: `proposed`, and it stays there until Anthony has read these words. He chose the SHAPE on 2026-08-11 — "a new requirement, mirroring KPPs" — when asked what need `cap:governance-proposal` serves (question:3f04e352bc497c5b). The wording below is an agent's draft of that shape, not his sentence, and `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` is the reason the distinction is being made explicitly rather than quietly resolved in the agent's favour.

THE SHAPE, deliberately mirroring `req:inviolable-intent` one layer along. That requirement says intent that must hold no matter what is recorded as inviolable, and a violation is COMPUTED, not remembered; `cap:kpp-proposal` is the capture half that asks the user whether something is a KPP rather than deciding for them. This is the same sentence about RULES rather than about intent, and `cap:governance-proposal` is its capture half. The parallel is the argument: a project's policy deserves the same treatment as its performance parameters, because both are things a person committed to and neither survives as prose.

WHAT IT REQUIRES, in three parts:
  (1) A rule is recordable as a design object rather than as a paragraph in a markdown file nobody diffs.
  (2) Its CONSEQUENCE — gate-blocking, advisory, or unstated — is the user's to state, never inherited. `DesignRule.enforced` is now genuinely three-state (schema/core.yaml:127, "Never defaulted"), so absence reads as "nobody has said" instead of as a choice.
  (3) A rule declared gate-blocking OWES a detector, and the debt is computed. That is `unverified_enforced_rule` at 0.6, and it is the part that stops governance-in-graph being prettier prose.

WHERE IT CAME FROM, recorded because this requirement exists partly BECAUSE that trace was missing. The demand signal is the GOVERNANCE-AS-DESIGN entry in dev_storyflow's `reflow2_feedback.md`, filed by api-boss (`5d608b85`) on 2026-08-08, carrying Anthony's own framing: "every project will be managed differently and have differing sets of people running it with their own practices and policies about merging and who can merge and other governing mechanisms — but allowing reflow2 to setup a generic set of nodes/edges that allow a user or set of users to define their own project management policies/governance in graph form is something that I think would be really helpful. additionally, by putting in graph form, you can start seeing issues and gaps in their policies (like we are experiencing in storyflow) and help resolve them properly."

⭐ WHY IT IS BEING WRITTEN NOW, MONTHS AFTER THE WORK SHIPPED. `cap:governance-proposal` was built, realized by `art:governance-proposal-skill`, and served to sessions while satisfying no requirement at all — surfaced as gap:3f04e352bc497c5b (unmotivated_capability, 0.55) and put to Anthony on 2026-08-11. Six sibling requirements from the same feedback entry DO exist and carry AUTHORED_BY to `who:storyflow-api-boss`; this one was the gap in that capture, not the whole of it. The honest reading is that the process ran and missed a step, not that the work was unrequested.

WHY NOT `req:defaults-do-not-assert`, considered and declined on 2026-08-11 by Anthony. That requirement names `DesignRule.enforced` explicitly and predates this skill by six weeks, so it is a genuine historical driver rather than a retro-fit. It was declined as the parent because it covers TEN defaulted-and-unread properties of which this addresses one, and because the default-asserting half has since been fixed in the schema — so a SATISFIES edge would make a tenth of that work read as delivered while nine properties stay untouched. It remains at `proposed` with nothing satisfying it.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not require any rule to be enforced — advisory is a first-class answer and six of reflow2's nine rules are advisory by the owner's explicit choice. It does not require every convention to be captured. And it says nothing about WHO may state a rule's consequence; that is `req:a-node-can-say-who-may-change-it`, still `proposed`.

HONEST BOUND: the capture half only helps a session that invokes the skill. A rule recorded by an agent that never loads `governance-proposal` still lands with `enforced` unstated — which is now reported rather than asserted, so the failure is visible, but it is not prevented.
